remainingEvidence: The authority half of the downward direction is now discriminated and stays uncited only because a planned row may carry no selectors: test/authority/scope-direction.test.ts proves against src/identity/scope.ts#scopePath and src/authority/runtime.ts#TenantAuthorityRuntime that the resolution path is the exact ordered ancestry and names no sibling or descendant; that a live allow Grant held at the Tenant or the Project reaches a Workspace beneath it at both validateBinding and check; that the same deny held at a sibling Workspace reaches nothing while one held at the Project does; that a Binding backed by a sibling's Grant is refused at src/authority/service.ts#requireBindingAuthority, at validateBinding, and by the closure src/authority/closure.ts asserts on every commit; and that an attenuation from a descendant is refused by Grant.canAttenuate, by createGrant, and by that same closure. The POLICY half is still absent: nothing asserts that declared PolicySet material — enforcement tiers, quotas, retention — resolves along the same path, and src/definition/policy.ts is W4, so a host resolving policy per-Workspace only would satisfy every current test

The composition conjunct is true by construction and unasserted, which is the direction a regression arrives from: src/facets/slot-store.ts#WorkspaceSlotCatalog reads a WorkspaceSlotStore and can only return the queried Workspace's own entries, so an ancestor's install cannot compose into a descendant today because no ancestor-scoped slot store exists. Closure needs the adversarial case — a Facet installed at the Tenant, a slot query at a Workspace beneath it, no entry returned — so the confinement survives the day a Tenant-scoped store is added

The Event conjunct cannot be proved by the matcher and has to be proved at the store that supplies candidate Subscriptions: src/workspaces/policy.ts#eventMatches compares kind, source and accepted trust only, so a Subscription (src/workspaces/subscription.ts#Subscription) whose pattern matches an Event accepted by a sibling or ancestor Actor exactly must still be shown never to receive it, and a mutation widening the candidate set past the accepting Actor must break a cited test

The positive cross-Scope path is untested as a Scope statement: a Tenant reacting to a Workspace Event must be shown to require a declared Subscription whose delivery authority is checked under C13-SUBSCRIPTION-AUTHORITY, and the same reaction must be impossible without that Subscription and its Grant, which is what separates a declared route from inherited visibility

The first of the two mutations this rule needs is now proven and the second is not. Narrowing the resolver's reach set in src/authority/runtime.ts#TenantAuthorityRuntime from the target's ancestry to the Scope holding the Grant turns the two positive reach tests red, and narrowing scopeReaches in the same file to an equality turns the validateBinding half red; both were applied, observed red, reverted, and observed green. The companion mutation — a slot entry or an Event that traverses the chain the way a Grant does — cannot be authored by W2: it needs src/facets/slot-store.ts (W3) and src/workspaces/{policy,subscription}.ts (W7)

remainingEvidence: The status is held at implemented rather than verified because this repair's evidence is written but not executed. The role pin is a wire change — identity.share-offer moves to codec major 2 and the SQLite projection gains a role_digest column — and the run that would execute the new memory and SQLite cases is reserved for integration under the parent's resource rule, so no measured pass exists in this worktree yet. Promotion needs that run and nothing else: the mechanism, the substrate projection and the hostile cases are all present
bounds: This rule does not claim that the subject named as issuer is the authenticated caller. issueShareOffer decides the administer-impact bound against the authority that named subject actually holds on the one durable Grant plane; binding a name to a caller is the section 8.5 dispatcher obligation evidenced by the C13-PROTOCOL-* atoms, exactly as every other AuthorityMutationService mutation names its subject as an argument.

The issuance bound is decided by one live allow Grant rather than by the union of the issuer's Grants. 'Bounded by what the issuer could have assigned directly' is read as the delegation bound Grant.canAttenuate already decides, and that bound names a single parent authority, so an issuer holding administer over two facet patterns through two separate Grants cannot issue an offer for a Role spanning both. Widening it to a union would be a second, weaker containment rule beside the attenuation one.

Issuer authority is decided once, at issuance. The offer that results carries no authority of its own, so a later redemption is governed by the offer's own terms rather than by the issuer's standing: the expiry window, the remaining bound and the offer's revocation state decide it, and an issuer whose administer Grant is revoked after issuance does not thereby stop a redemption. What such a revocation does reach is the Memberships already minted, which are revoked as Memberships and advance their own path epochs. Nothing here claims that a redemption re-checks the issuer.

The Role pin compares exact canonical Role bytes rather than a subset relation, so a narrowing change to a Role refuses an open offer exactly as a widening one does, and changing a Role back to byte-identical content makes its offers redeemable again. That is the intended reading of 'the Role the issuer authorised': an offer names one exact Role content, not a family of Roles a later editor considers no wider.

changeRole neither scans nor closes open offers. A widened Role leaves every open offer for it refusing at redemption rather than revoked, which keeps a global template edit off an unbounded offer scan and keeps the refusal on the path that mints authority. An offer refused this way is not repaired: an issuer with current authority issues a new offer against the new Role content.

Cross-Tenant identity is not reclassified by this rule. A ForeignPrincipalRef remains the valid cross-Tenant form and keeps its guest-trust evidence path; what issueShareOffer and redeemShareOffer refuse is a local PrincipalRef naming another Tenant, which is a malformed local subject rather than a guest, and each refusal is the stable authority.denied rather than a leaked constructor TypeError.
